samples.summary: The composite link-exit rule is hand-copied into three editors; only the primitive is shared
samples.evidence: `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` was correctly hoisted into `model/caret-style.ts`, but the *rule built on it* — "exitsLink = isAtLinkTrailingEdge(doc, pos) || (prev pending already holds href: undefined) ⇒ spread `href: undefined` onto the seed" — is written out three separate times: `pendingStyleFor` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts ~1193), `TextEditor.setPendingStyleGuarded` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts ~3465) and inline in `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl` (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts ~888-902). The copies already differ (editor.ts exempts a write that names `href`; the text-box copy reads its local `staged` instead of `pending.get()`; the text-editor copy has no exemption at all). `model/caret-style.ts:1-11` itself records that hand-copied caret logic drifting between these same three editors is how #715 shipped, so the repo's own doctrine argues for one shared `pendingStyleWithLinkExit(doc, pos, prev, seed)` helper beside `isAtLinkTrailingEdge`. Cost today is internal (behaviour is consistent), but the next change to the rule must be made in three files.

samples.summary: Slides/board toolbar design doc not updated for the new Remove link button; the slides behaviour is filed under a Docs-area doc instead
samples.evidence: `slides-toolbar-redesign.md` is the canonical doc for the slides text-edit toolbar: §"State 3 — Text editing" enumerates the button row (`[B] [I] [U] [Aa Color ▾] [🔗 Link]`, line 247) and its source table says the group is "Shared `text-format-group.tsx`, rendered with `showStrikethrough={false}` and `showHighlight={false}`" (line 254); line 260 repeats it for the mobile `TextFormatSheet`. The change adds a third flag (`showRemoveLink`) and a new button to both surfaces (and, via `board-toolbar.tsx:444` reusing `TextEditSection`, to Board too — see also `docs/design/board/board-editing-parity.md`), but records it only in `docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md` ("Removing a link on slides", ~line 340). Per CONTRIBUTING/README the change belongs folded into the canonical subsystem doc; as filed, the slides toolbar doc is now stale and the slides behaviour is documented in a Docs font-controls doc.

samples.summary: New collapsed-caret pending-style invariant not recorded in the pending-style design doc
samples.evidence: `docs-pending-inline-style.md` is the canonical doc for the pending/stored-mark contract; §Architecture (lines 54-61) explicitly describes the two collapsed-caret write surfaces (`editor.applyStyle`/`clearInlineFormatting` and `text-editor.toggleStyle`/`clearFormatting`) and their shared contract. This change adds a new, cross-cutting invariant to exactly that contract — every collapsed-caret seed derived from the caret style must re-arm `href: undefined` at a link trailing edge, because `pending.set` replaces rather than merges — plus a third seed site in `text-box-editor.stepSelectionFontSize`. None of it is written into this doc; it lives only in `docs-font-controls.md`. A reader of the pending-style doc adding a fourth collapsed-caret seed would not learn the rule.

samples.summary: Cmd+\ silently gains font/colour clearing — a user-visible behaviour change beyond the hyperlink issue
samples.evidence: Replacing `clearFormatting`'s hand-rolled list with `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3440/3445) does more than stop deleting `href`: the shortcut now also clears `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, `color` and `backgroundColor`, which it never did. That is a defensible drift fix and is documented in `docs-font-controls.md`, but it is scope beyond "Clear formatting must not remove hyperlinks", it changes what Cmd+\ does for every user, and the end-user docs that list the shortcut (`packages/documentation/docs-editor/keyboard-shortcuts.md:73`, `docs-editor/writing-a-document.md:74`) are untouched. Worth an explicit call-out in the issue/PR rather than riding along.

samples.summary: Shared `removeLink` contract now means two different things depending on the implementation
samples.evidence: The shared interface's new doc says "A selection takes precedence over the caret where the implementation supports one" (types.ts:94-104). The docs `EditorAPI.removeLink` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3737-3755) is still caret-only, while `TextBoxEditorAPI.removeLink` (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1252-1285) is now selection-first. The single shared `Remove link` button in `text-format-group.tsx` therefore behaves differently per surface, and the interface enshrines the divergence rather than resolving it. Either lift the selection-first branch into the docs editor too (it is the same two-line check) or state one contract; as written the shared component's behaviour is implementation-defined.

samples.summary: Slides gains a Remove link button beside an Insert link button that cannot insert a link
samples.evidence: `TextFormatGroup` defaults `showLink` to true and slides/board do not override it, so the slides text-edit toolbar already renders an Insert link button whose `requestLink()` reaches an unwired `onLinkRequest` (see the diff's own comment at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:736-750: "Cmd+K no-ops at the editor level until then, so *inserting* a link here is not yet possible"). Placing a working Remove link next to a dead Insert link is an incoherent surface: the pair reads as a link toolbar where half of it silently does nothing. Either hide Insert link on slides (`showLink={false}`) or note in the design doc why the dead control stays.

samples.summary: End-user docs not updated for the new Remove link control on slides/board text editing
samples.evidence: `packages/documentation/board/using-the-board.md:77-80` enumerates the text-edit toolbar ("font family and size, bold, italic, underline, text color, clear formatting, paragraph alignment, …") and board reuses `TextEditSection` (packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-toolbar.tsx:444), which now renders Remove link. The slides/docs user docs likewise still describe Clear formatting without noting that it now preserves hyperlinks. Purely documentation drift, no behavioural cost.

samples.summary: `removeLink` declared optional although every implementor provides it
samples.evidence: `removeLink?(): void` is optional "so a surface that renders no Remove-link control need not supply it", yet both implementors (docs `EditorAPI`, `SlidesTextBoxEditor` at packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:270) have it, and the call site uses `editor.removeLink?.()` — so a surface that forgets to implement it fails silently instead of at the type boundary. Given packages/frontend has no `tsc` gate, the optional marker plus optional call removes the only signal that would have caught a missing implementation.
